arxiv-2102-07987.title: The Elliptical Potential Lemma for General Distributions with an Application to Linear Thompson Sampling
arxiv-2102-07987.creator: Nima Hamidi, Mohsen Bayati
arxiv-2102-07987.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Nima Hamidi, Mohsen Bayati. In this note, we introduce a general version of the well-known elliptical potential lemma that is a widely used technique in the analysis of algorithms in sequential learning and decision-making problems. We consider a stochastic linear bandit setting where a decision-maker sequentially chooses among a set of given actions, observes their noisy rewards, and aims to maximize her cumulative expected reward over a decision-making horizon.

arxiv-2108-07905.title: Galois Groups in Enumerative Geometry and Applications Thanks: Research of Sottile and Yahl supported by grant 636314 from the Simons Foundation.
arxiv-2108-07905.creator: Frank Sottile, Thomas Yahl
arxiv-2108-07905.description: Abstract . As Jordan observed in 1870, just as univariate polynomials have Galois groups, so do problems in enumerative geometry. Despite this pedigree, the study of Galois groups in enumerative geometry was dormant for a century, with a systematic study only occuring in the past 15 years. We discuss the current directions of this study, including open problems and conjectures.

arxiv-2206-06437.title: Distribution of Quantum Circuits Over General Quantum Networks
arxiv-2206-06437.creator: Ranjani G. Sundaram, Himanshu Gupta, C. R. Ramakrishnan
arxiv-2206-06437.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ranjani G. Sundaram, Himanshu Gupta, C. R. Ramakrishnan. Near-term quantum computers can hold only a small number of qubits. One way to facilitate large-scale quantum computations is through a distributed network of quantum computers. In this work, we consider the problem of distributing quantum programs represented as quantum circuits across a quantum network of heterogeneous quantum computers, in a way that minimizes the overall communication cost required to execute the distributed circuit.

arxiv-2303-08857.title: Phase transition kinetics revealed in laser-heated dynamic diamond anvil cells
arxiv-2303-08857.creator: Matthew Ricks, Arianna E. Gleason, Francesca Miozzi, Hong Yang, Stella Chariton, Vitali B. Prakapenka, Stanislav V. Sinogeikin, Richard L. Sandberg, Wendy L. Mao, Silvia Pandolfi
arxiv-2303-08857.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Matthew Ricks, Arianna E. Gleason, Francesca Miozzi, Hong Yang, Stella Chariton, Vitali B. Prakapenka, Stanislav V. Sinogeikin, Richard L. Sandberg, Wendy L. Mao, Silvia Pandolfi. We report on a novel approach to dynamic compression of materials that bridges the gap between previous static- and dynamic- compression techniques, allowing to explore a wide range of pathways in the pressure-temperature space.

arxiv-2305-05654.title: Using Knowledge Units of Programming Languages to Recommend Reviewers for Pull Requests: An Empirical Study
arxiv-2305-05654.creator: Md Ahasanuzzaman, Gustavo A. Oliva, Ahmed E. Hassan
arxiv-2305-05654.description: Abstract Code review is a key element of quality assurance in software development. Determining the right reviewer for a given code change requires understanding the characteristics of the changed code, identifying the skills of each potential reviewer (expertise profile), and finding a good match between the two.

arxiv-2305-11358.title: Understanding the World to Solve Social Dilemmas using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2305-11358.creator: Manuel Sebastián Ríos & Nicanor Quijano, Luis Felipe Giraldo
arxiv-2305-11358.description: Abstract Social dilemmas are situations where groups of individuals can benefit from mutual cooperation but conflicting interests impede them from doing so. This type of situations resembles many of humanity’s most critical challenges, and discovering mechanisms that facilitate the emergence of cooperative behaviors is still an open problem.

arxiv-2311-09921.title: Revisiting the evidence for precession in GW200129 with machine learning noise mitigation
arxiv-2311-09921.creator: Ronaldas Macas, Andrew Lundgren, Gregory Ashton
arxiv-2311-09921.description: Abstract GW200129 is claimed to be the first-ever observation of the spin-disk orbital precession detected with gravitational waves (GWs) from an individual binary system. However, this claim warrants a cautious evaluation because the GW event coincided with a broadband noise disturbance in LIGO Livingston caused by the 45 MHz electro-optic modulator system.

arxiv-2407-12141.title: Predicting Emotion Intensity in Polish Political Texts: Comparing Supervised Models and Large Language Models in a Resource-Poor Language
arxiv-2407-12141.creator: Hubert Plisiecki, Piotr Koc, Maria Flakus, Artur Pokropek
arxiv-2407-12141.description: Abstract This study explores the use of large language models (LLMs) to predict emotion intensity in Polish political texts, a resource-poor language context. The research compares the performance of several LLMs against a supervised model trained on an annotated corpus of 10,000 social media texts, evaluated for the intensity of emotions by expert judges.

arxiv-2408-07849.title: Molecular gas budget of strongly magnified low-mass star-forming galaxies at cosmic noon
arxiv-2408-07849.creator: V. Catán, J. González-López, M. Solimano, L. F. Barrientos, A. Afruni, M. Aravena, M. Bayliss, J. A. Hernández, C. Ledoux, G. Mahler, K. Sharon, N. Tejos
arxiv-2408-07849.description: Abstract Aims. The aim of this study is to investigate the molecular gas content of strongly magnified low-mass star-forming galaxies (SFGs) around the cosmic noon period ( z ∼ 2 z\sim 2 ) through observations of carbon monoxide (CO) emission lines and dust continuum emission, both of which serve as tracers of molecular gas (H 2 ). arxiv-2509-02288.title: Paving the way to a 𝖳 \operatorname{\mathsf{T}} -coercive method for the wave equation
arxiv-2509-02288.creator: Daniel Hoonhout, Richard Löscher, Carolina Urzúa-Torres
arxiv-2509-02288.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Daniel Hoonhout, Richard Löscher, Carolina Urzúa-Torres. In this paper, we take a first step toward introducing a space-time transformation operator 𝖳 \operatorname{\mathsf{T}} that establishes 𝖳 \operatorname{\mathsf{T}} -coercivity for the weak variational formulation of the wave equation in space and time on bounded Lipschitz domains. As a model problem, we study the ordinary differential equation (ODE) u ′′ + μ ​ u = f u^{\prime\prime}+\mu u=f for μ > 0 \mu>0 , which is linked to the wave equation via a Fourier expansion in space.

pmc-10505181.title: Organic walled microfossils in wet peperites from the early Cretaceous Paraná-Etendeka volcanism of Brazil
pmc-10505181.creator: Lucas Del Mouro, Bruno Becker-Kerber, Valdecir A Janasi, Marcelo de Araújo Carvalho, Breno L Waichel, Evandro F Lima, Lucas M M Rossetti, Vinicius Cruz, Mateus Souza Silva, Natália Famelli, Javier Ortega-Hernández
pmc-10505181.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Large igneous provinces (LIPs) are major magmatic events that have a significant impact on the global environment and the biosphere, for example as triggers of mass extinctions. LIPs provide an excellent sedimentological and geochemical record of short but intense periods of geological activity in the past, but their contribution towards understanding ancient life is much more restricted due to the destructive nature of their igneous origin.

pmc-10567211.title: Rare Lymphoma of the Breast: A Case Report
pmc-10567211.creator: Megan Bradley, Katie Kirk, Jayati Mallick, Flavia E Posleman Monetto
pmc-10567211.description: Lymphoma of the breast is a rare malignancy of the breast lymphoid tissue. It can present as either a primary or a secondary malignancy due to metastasis from a systemic disease. Secondary breast lymphoma (SBL) is one of the most common malignancies to metastasize to the breast.

pmc-11600937.title: Bioinformatics Analysis and Experimental Validation to Identify Key Glycosylation-Related Genes in Asthma
pmc-11600937.creator: Yue Li, Ruhao Wu, Xiaoying Tian, Mengting Zhang, Zhe Cheng
pmc-11600937.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PurposeAsthma is a chronic inflammatory disease influenced by complex genetic and environmental factors. Despite extensive research, the intricate pathophysiology of asthma remains incompletely understood. Furthermore, the effects of glycosylation on asthma remain unclear.

pmc-11712047.title: Clinical and epidemiological baseline characterization of dementia cases in a specialized center in Recife
pmc-11712047.creator: Mariana Albuquerque de Luna, Camila Oliveira Negri, Bruna Cristina de Oliveira Lima, João Augusto de Macedo Cavalcanti de Albuquerque, Bárbara Nascimento Moutinho, Ilo de Vasconcelos Ximenes Júnior, Mariana Leandro Silva, Tatiana Caldas Neves da Silva, Barbara Matos Almeida Queiroz, Breno José Alenc
pmc-11712047.description: IntroductionDementia numbers are increasing rapidly with a substantial contribution from low and middle‐income countries. There’s a limited number of reports in Brazil, mostly modest initiatives from south‐eastern, more developed regions. With a population of approximately 1.6 million individuals, Recife is among the largest cities of Northeast Brazil, a region of steep social disparities and high prevalence of low‐literacy.

pmc-12387558.title: Evaluating the Assembly Strategy of a Fungal Genome from Metagenomic Data: Solorina crocea (Peltigerales, Ascomycota) as a Case Study
pmc-12387558.creator: Ana García-Muñoz, Raquel Pino-Bodas
pmc-12387558.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The advent of next-generation sequencing technologies has given rise to considerably diverse techniques. However, integrating data from these technologies to generate high-quality genomes remains challenging, particularly when starting from metagenomic data. To provide further insight into this process, the genome of the lichenized fungus Solorina crocea was sequenced using DNA extracted from the thallus, which contains the genome of the mycobiont, along with those of the photobionts (a green alga and a cyanobacterium), and other associated microorganisms.

pmc-12520818.title: Gene Expression in Urinary Sediment Cells as an Indicator of the Contribution of Plasma Lipids to Diabetic Kidney Disease
pmc-12520818.creator: Thaina Tavolaro Zocchio, Aritania Souza Santos, Ana Mercedes Cavaleiro, Luiz Henrique Gomes Matheus, Monique de Fátima Mello Santana, Eduarda Palanca, Ariana Tito Rodrigues, Milena Gomes Vancini, Márcia Nery, Marisa Passarelli, Maria Lúcia Corrêa-Giannella
pmc-12520818.description: BackgroundIn individuals with Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1D) who maintain good glycemic control and are free of chronic complications, lipid profiles are generally within normal ranges. However, impaired renal function or albuminuria alters this profile, contributing to the progression of diabetic kidney disease (DKD).

pmc-12527932.title: NOX1 and NPY1R mark regional colon stem cell populations that serve as cancer origins in vivo
pmc-12527932.creator: Maxime Gasnier, Tanysha Chi-Ying Chen, Swathi Yada, Sowmya Sagiraju, Yusuke Yoshikawa, Stefano Perna, Hui Yi Grace Lim, Bernett Lee, Nick Barker
pmc-12527932.description: Current colorectal cancer mouse models either lack colon specificity, limiting progression towards more advanced disease, or preclude evaluation of resident stem cells as cancer origins. Here we report the identification of NOX1 and NPY1R as cell-surface markers enriched in LGR5+ stem cells predominantly within the caecum and exclusively within the middle and distal colorectum, respectively.

pmc-13176203.title: Effects of remote breastfeeding guidance on breastfeeding rates and neonatal health: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13176203.creator: Miaomiao Hu, Sang Sang, Hui Pei, Xiao Han, Qiqi Wei, Li Wei, Ji Qi, Jing Li
pmc-13176203.description: BackgroundBreastfeeding is widely acknowledged as the optimal feeding method for neonatal health. Remote breastfeeding guidance (e.g., using the telephone, text messages, mobile applications, and so on) may improve breastfeeding rates and neonatal outcomes, but its short-term impact and effect across economic regions remain unclear.

pmc-13286362.title: Amoeboid cancer cells at a glance
pmc-13286362.creator: Ritobrata Ghose, Victoria Sanz-Moreno
pmc-13286362.description: Amoeboid behaviour represents a distinct and clinically significant cancer cell state within the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) spectrum. Defined by the loss of cell–cell junctions and adoption of a rounded morphology, amoeboid cancer cells exhibit low adhesion and rely heavily on Rho–ROCK–myosin II-mediated cortical contractility.

pmc-13382062.title: Self-assembled meniscus-specific ECM membrane promotes cell migration and vascular ingrowth for meniscus repair and reconstruction
pmc-13382062.creator: Mingze Du, Yuwei Wang, Tuo Wu, Huinan Lai, Liya Ai, Jiajun Liu, Ting Zhu, Jingke Du, Jun Yin, Dong Jiang
pmc-13382062.description: BackgroundThe knee meniscus has limited intrinsic repair and regenerative capacity. Safe and effective biotherapeutic products remain lacking, and enhancing cell migration and angiogenesis remains a major challenge. This study aimed to develop a novel self-assembled meniscus-specific extracellular matrix membrane (saECM-M) and evaluate its performance in scaffold-free meniscus repair and scaffold-guided whole-meniscus reconstruction, in comparison with chemically processed decellularized ECM (cpd-ECM).
